extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and practitioners handling ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for filing statements and proposing amendments to patents during USPTO reexamination (ex parte and inter partes), including timing, format, markings, service, and limitations on amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Director for denial of reexamination (37 CFR 1.515(c), 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.515(c) and 1.181 to challenge a denial of reexamination must be filed within one month of the mailing date of the decision denying the request for reexamination. Extensions of time to file such a petition may only be sought by a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with appropriate fee to waive the time provisions of 37 CFR 1.515(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on petitions under 37 CFR 1.515(c) are final and not appealable. 37 CFR 1.515(c) applies only to challenging a basis for denying reexamination, not to challenging a basis for granting reexamination. If an order grants reexamination as to some claims but finds no SNQ for others, a third-party requester may petition under 1.515(c) within one month to reconsider the determination as to the claim for which no SNQ was found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial refund of reexamination filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: After the time to petition has expired without a petition filed, or a petition has been filed and the decision affirms denial, a partial refund of the filing fee for requesting reexamination will be made to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund authority: 35 U.S.C. 303(c) and 37 CFR 1.26(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement timing (37 CFR 1.530)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner in an ex parte reexamination shall be filed prior to determinations under § 1.515 or § 1.520; premature statements will not be acknowledged or considered and will be returned or discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reexamination is ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 the order will set a period of not less than two months for the patent owner to file a statement and any narrowing amendments; extensions may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). Any statement must clearly point out why the patent claims are believed patentable considering the cited prior art alone or in reasonable combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of patent owner statement on requester
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the patent owner’s statement must be served on the requester, unless the request was filed by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of service is required (37 CFR 1.530(c)); lack of proof of service may prompt CRU to contact the patent owner to submit supplemental proof, or to contact the requester to verify service. If the 2-month period under 1.530 expires and the requester has not been served, the patent owner’s statement may be considered inappropriate and denied consideration (see 37 CFR 1.248 and MPEP § 2267).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester reply deadline (37 CFR 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for response by requester for a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 is two months from the patent owner’s service date, not two months from the date the patent owner’s statement was received in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate requester reply deadline based on date of service to requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of patent owner’s statement program
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may waive the right to file a patent owner’s statement to expedite reexamination; the CRU will contact the patent owner by telephone to request the optional waiver after a filing date has been granted and before examiner review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone communication must be strictly limited to requesting waiver and recording agreement/non-agreement; discussion of merits is not permitted. The CRU will record the communication on form PTOL-2292 and mail copies to patent owner and any third-party requester. If the patent owner agrees, the examiner may issue the reexamination order and the first Office action on the merits the same day or shortly thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530 (and comply with formal presentation requirements in 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments submitted must include required fees (37 CFR 1.20(c)) and follow the specific rules for specification, claims, and drawings as set out in 1.530(d)-(j). Noncompliant amendments may be held inappropriate or not entered; see form paragraphs PTOL-22.12/22.13 and instructions for informing the patent owner and time to correct informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment format (37 CFR 1.530(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the specification (other than claims) must be made by submission of the full text of any paragraph to be changed, with markings showing changes (single brackets for deletions and underlining for additions), and the precise point in the specification where the change is to be made must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception allowing deletion of an entire paragraph by statement alone is permitted, but presenting the full text aids entry. Underlining for added paragraphs must be the complete text. Markings are made vis-a-vis the original patent, not relative to prior amendments. Indicate precise insertion point to avoid delays in issuance of reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment format (37 CFR 1.530(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim proposed to be amended, the entire text of the claim must be presented with appropriate markings; for each proposed new claim, the entire text must be presented and underlined throughout; cancellation of a claim is by a direction to cancel the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be presented whether submitted on paper or compact disc. Examiner’s amendments at NIRC stage also require full claim text with markings. A proposed new claim previously added can be canceled by direction. Failure to present full text and markings may result in informality or non-entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status requirement (37 CFR 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, the submission must supply, on separate pages, the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and of all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure for the changes to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status will generally result in an informal notification (MPEP § 2266.02) and amendments submitted after final rejection will not be entered. The explanation of support addresses the merits; failure to provide it will likewise lead to notification and possible non-entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings conventions (37 CFR 1.530(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter to be omitted must be enclosed in single brackets; the matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bracketing and underlining are made with respect to the original patent text (not prior amendments). When reexamination certificate is printed, underlined matter is shown in italics and brackets printed as inserted during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preserved (37 CFR 1.530(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims may not be renumbered; a patent claim retains its number even if canceled, and any added claims must be numbered to follow the highest-numbered original patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new claims added earlier are later canceled, claim numbers for remaining new claims will be renumbered at NIRC preparation to follow original patent claims. A claim number previously assigned to a now-canceled new claim should not be reassigned during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope; no new matter (37 CFR 1.530(j) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter; no amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Amendments that broaden claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test for enlargement is the same as for reissue applications under 35 U.S.C. 251 (see In re Freeman and MPEP § 2258). For handling of new matter see MPEP § 2270. Amendments are normally entered if timely and rule-compliant, but do not become effective in the patent until the reexamination certificate is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of amendments tied to reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments entered during prosecution are not effective to alter the patent until issuance of the certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307. No amendment (other than cancellation) will be incorporated into a patent if the certificate issues after patent expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in expired patents prohibited (37 CFR 1.530(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent; if a patent expires during reexamination, all amendments to the patent claims and all claims added during the proceeding are withdrawn and subsequent reexamination proceeds on the unamended claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the time of NIRC preparation, examiner should ensure all rejected and objected-to claims are canceled; cancellation of original patent claims is the only amendatory change permitted in an expired patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal paper and formatting requirements (37 CFR 1.52(a),(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers that become part of the permanent USPTO records must be on suitable paper (A4 or 8.5x11), one side only, specified minimum margins (top 2.0 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 2.0 cm, bottom 2.0 cm), plain white, written in permanent dark ink or machine print, and presented with sufficient clarity and contrast for reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should have no holes, must be same size sheets not permanently bound, and must meet e-filing formatting if submitted electronically. The application/proceeding must be in English or accompanied by an accurate English translation. Specification text requirements (lines 1.5 or double spaced, nonscript font like Arial/Times Roman/Courier, preferred font size 12, capital letters at least 0.3175 cm but not smaller than 0.21 cm) and single column text apply except where exceptions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and abstract placement requirements (37 CFR 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page; the abstract must commence on a separate sheet or be the first page of the patent in reissue or reexamination or supplemental examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 1.75(h) and 1.72(b) for page/electronic placement conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; upon approval, file new sheets in compliance with § 1.84, identify amended figures as 'Amended', new figures as 'New', and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.84 for drawing standards; amended figures must be identified and follow the same formal requirements as other amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim (not in the original patent) must be presented with underlining throughout the claim, including the claim number and status indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added claims must be numbered beginning with the next higher number than the number of claims in the original patent; if new claims added earlier are later canceled, remaining new claims will be renumbered at NIRC preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of new claims (presentation and remarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a new claim previously presented in the reexamination must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material and must be underlined throughout; the presentation cannot contain bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because changes are made vis-a-vis the original patent, the amended new claim does not show prior-version differences; the patent owner must point out what changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment. As required by 37 CFR 1.530(e), each change must be accompanied by explanation of support in the disclosure for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple amendments to original claims must incorporate prior changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one amendment to an original patent claim is made, each subsequent amendment must include the changes previously presented as well as the new changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: first amendment shows earlier change (e.g., replace 'cutting means' with 'knife'), second amendment must include that prior change text plus the new change (e.g., 'serrated'). This ensures the submitted claim text is the full current text with all amendments shown vis-a-vis the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for improper amendments and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) prior to final rejection, a supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments is required; if not timely corrected, the amendment may be held not to be an appropriate response and prosecution terminated leading to issuance of a reexamination certificate. After final rejection, informality notices and non-entry procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs PTOL-22.13 or PTOL-475 for advising patent owner of informality prior to final rejection. After final rejection, do not use PTOL-22.13 or PTOL-475; instead issue an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) indicating the amendment was not entered and explain the noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments require full text (no 1.121(g) exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner's amendments made at the time the NIRC is prepared require the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed with markings; the exception for examiner’s amendment in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply to examiner’s amendments in reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies regardless of submission medium (paper or compact disc).
